items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And Kenny Clarke, he came through St. Louis and played with Jeter- Pillars for a long time... He was one of the first members of the Modern Jazz Quartet, MJQ.

ctx.x: Bill Coleman, Stuff Smith, Kenny Drew, Kenny Clarke, Johnny Griffin is still living but he’s still over there in Europe. You get some much, you’re appreciated so much over there.
Were you ever tempted to settle there permanently?

items.title: 52031_Kenny Clarke oral history interview
items.q: So we joined the band -- No, I think Harry was in the band, I guess, oh, maybe a couple of days before I was. I joined the band.

ctx.x: So anyway, Wilbur Kirk, he was so wonderful, you know, said, "Well, come on, Kenny, try." So there was Harry Edison, who was 17 years old at the time, and when I left to go I took him with me, and his mother said -- he's from Columbus, Ohio. So his mother says, "Kenny, look out for
Harry, because I was a little older than Harry." So I said, "Well, don't worry, Mrs. Edison."
